reviews.title: Extremely helpful!!!
reviews.text: This app is basically Home Chef or Hello Fresh without food being delivered to your house.  This app is great for families, single living or if your just living with your partner and have no clue what to make or want speedy recipes for the week that are healthy/comforting and fit your budget.  Yes there is a subscription, but you get a 3 day free trial and it’s $10 monthly or $50 annually.  Not bad when just trying to find your footing in the kitchen.  It caters to the store you shop at, weekly budget, food restrictions and dietary restrictions as well.  Even gives you a shopping list with recipe instructions and the nutrition information.  Completely recommend.

reviews.title: A good start, but needs work
reviews.text: This application contains good menus with a wide range of cuisines, but it is not as usable as it might be. The workflow starts by providing a selection of meals for a period of time, matching your dietary profile. From there, you can edit the menu, but the fact that you can do this is not obvious from the UI. Once you generate a shopping list, there’s no way to lock the list of menu items to the shopping list, so it’s easy to accidentally modify that menu. If you already use an alternate shopping list, it’s very difficult to transfer the list from this application to another one. Marking a meal “cooked“ produces no visual change in the list of menu items. Once you start cooking, the app really falls apart. I find myself constantly, switching back-and-forth between the ingredients view and the instructions, and the instruction flow does not actually match the kitchen flow very well. Three examples: 1. I have a selected recipe that takes 2 1/2 hours to make because of a 2 hour required marination time, but that is not reflected in the prep time.  2. I just finished executing a recipe that requires adding ingredients to boiling pasta, but that step is four or five steps down in the recipe, after the pasta is complete. 3. None of the recipes include the amount of herbs and spices; you have to pluck that off the ingredients list. The developers would do well to examine an application like MealLime, or a cookbook like Joy of Cooking, to see how this can be alleviated.

reviews.title: Dietary Restrictions/Requirements.
reviews.text:
1.  It only lets you select one dietary restriction. What if you need gluten free and vegetarian?    Said select all that apply but only allowed me to select one.  
2. What if you only have one person with a dietary restriction?  If you select vegetarian, gluten free, ect it assumes all meals must be 100% that dietary requirement. In my house we have 1 vegetarian and 3 carnivores so this app isn’t much help. I have to plan 2 meal plans. What I would like is something that plans a meal plan for the entire family.  If 1 of 4 is vegetarian have a meal plan with a meat entree, a vegetarian entree that could double as a side, a 2nd vegetable side and a whatever else is in the plan for that meal. To do this though the app needs to ask how many of the family members have the dietary restrictions, then plans meals that can fit. 
It seems the app would be pretty good for those with households that don’t need more than 1 dietary restriction or mixed dietary requirements.

reviews.title: Great, but could be much better
reviews.text:
The ingredients list needs to be much more specific - listing “cooked chicken” doesn’t tell me what kind of chicken I need to buy and I shouldn’t have to dig into the cooking instructions to figure it out. Same with “mozzarella” - shredded, block, ball, pearled?

Another thing I don’t like is that because it’s randomized when creating a menu for a week, I sometimes get five consecutive meal suggestions where the protein is all salmon or chicken. It’s an easy fix to pin the ones I like and then redraw for the meals I don’t want, but I feel like that can and should be better accounted for in the app’s design.

Would also be really nice if the app integrated directly with my grocery store’s (Meijer) app, so that I can just click and add the ingredients to the Meijer cart directly from the app, without having to switch between apps over and over, adding things to the Meijer cart individually.

reviews.title: Awesome for someone who doesn’t have kids or isn’t on a strict diet
reviews.text: This app is really good for simple meals and a little bit of customization. It offers a lot of utility for a quick and easy meals and can save you lots of money. However, the reason for the three out of five stars is because if you’re on a diet such as keto 30 or anything like that, there is no way for you to actually custom build that it also asks for your preferences whether you want protein or gut friendly meals, etc. but completely ignores those preferences when building out your weekly meal plan. This is really great for when you’re getting started as a beginner meal planner but beyond that it’s hard to see this as an option for someone who has a bigger family and who’s on a specific diet

reviews.title: Accurate pricing to store price!!
reviews.text: This app has saved so much time and took away the time it takes me to sit down and think of meals for the week! They give you a grocery list to shop for the items you need for your meals at your preferred store. Also the pricing is on point to the price at my store. It was only off by $0.25 which is totally fine with me, especially with one of my meals being steak for the week! I gave it a $150 budget but the meal plan for the week was only $108. And that meal plan included things like a steak and peppercorn sauce, Chicken Caesar wrap, Spaghetti Bolognese, BBQ loaded chicken wrap, homemade burgers, and a chili cheese beef pasta! My plan I for 3 people! So this is awesome!

reviews.title: Random selection style choices
reviews.text: It’s fine, has some options but you can’t really dig into what you want. I noticed too that preferences arent also followed (like giving me recipes that call for an air fryer when i said i didnt have one or offering dairy options when i said no dairy), so just be aware of those things. Not sure if it’s worth the price point with how much work it is to get a meal within your preferences, or how often you have to skip a meal to get something you want. The idea is great, just think there should be more preferences or a list of recipes that you can go through a favorite and the app put them in your deck of choices.

reviews.title: Minimal Selections
reviews.text: I would say that the app is getting somewhere and very convenient but it’s also missing the flexibility of diets. I was trying to see if I could do a meal plan that was close to being keto and lower in calories while having a high packed protein meal, and it definitely was able to account for high protein and low calories, but couldn’t find anything good for keto. Also the app should let you select more grocery store options (also missing Sam’s club.) I also wanted to see if I could edit some of the meals but that option wasn’t available. Definitely do like how the app is but needs more work.

reviews.title: Kinda minimal
reviews.text: Overall as far as giving you a baseline of what you might want to make for your meals it does a good job. But on the other hand the recipes are very minimal and if you made them the way the recipes are laid out the food would not be very good. There are no spices listed other than salt and pepper. I found each recipe I made I had to do quite a bit of doctoring up. But I did like knowing I had a plan for the week, even if I had to be creative and figure out how I was going to make it work for me and my family’s taste.

reviews.title: Okay
reviews.text: Look don’t get me wrong it’s useful, assistance with meal planner the whole 9 yards. 10 bucks a month for AI generated meal plans doesn’t seem worth it. Chat GPT is the same and will assistance with meal planning the same way as this will. I would gladly pay 2 dollars a month for this. But 10 is a stretch, people will say it’s only 10 dollars, but that’s also on of everything other companies subscription top of this charge. So obviously whom ever created this probably made the UI in a week, and is making thousands a dollars a month from our subscription plans. I’ll probably use this app for a week cancel and save all the recipes. That’s what I would recommend.
